analysis.title: Morning Market Tidbits: Jobs data cast their vote for resilience
key_insights: This week's labor indicators point to continued resilience, with little evidence of a meaningful deterioration.
BofA forecasts a 75k Oct payroll gain (private 70k) and a flat 4.2% unemployment rate, versus consensus of 65k payrolls (private 64k).

Unfavorable October seasonals and softer high-frequency hiring indicators pose downside risk to BofA's payroll call, but even a modest miss would likely leave job growth above breakeven with little change in the unemployment rate.
BofA expects markets and the Fed to stay focused on inflation in assessing the case for a December hike, because the labor market looks stable.
ADP showed private-sector job growth of +86k in Oct, unchanged from Sep. Initial claims remain exceptionally benign.
Challenger layoff announcements were the lowest for the month of October since 2023.
Sep JOLTS was hawkish on the margin, with job openings and vacancies per unemployed worker (1.06) picking up.
Bank of America Institute data point to slower y/y job growth in Oct, but with little sign of labor-market stress.
BofA's 3Q26 GDP tracking estimate rose one tenth to 3.8% q/q saar after the September trade balance, matching its official forecast of 3.4% only loosely (official forecast is 3.4%).
Today's events: Oct jobs report at 8:30, University of Michigan sentiment at 10:00, and comments from Fed officials Williams, Musalem and Bowman.

tension_points.bull_case: Labor indicators show resilience, and BofA forecasts a 75k payroll gain, above the 65k consensus.
tension_points.bear_case: Unfavorable October seasonals and softer high-frequency hiring indicators pose downside risk to the payroll call.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A payroll print well below BofA's 75k forecast, beyond a modest miss that would still leave job growth above breakeven, or a rise in the unemployment rate from 4.2%.
